messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: alert: p95 latency spike detected on /v1/generate (p95 ~1200ms, error-rate +0.8%). dashboard: https://grafana.internal/d/abc123

sam oncall: i'm paged — pulling logs and queues. seeing queue depth climb on realtime pool. probe shows batch-wait ms rising past 40ms average.

maria infra: GPUs on shards 2/5 at 98% and there are lots of kv-cache misses. traffic pattern unchanged but per-shard qps skewed toward small-quant model-4-small-quant.

lee ml-runtime: quick hypothesis: continuous batching window grew under burst, causing head-of-line latency for low-latency routes. bigger batches => some requests starved. also large-context requests elongating kernels.

sam oncall: propose low-risk live mitigations (non-disruptive, reversible):
- apply soft global ingress QPS limit to non-SLA customers (free & trial) to reduce pressure
- shrink continuous batching window for realtime /generate route from 20ms -> 8ms
- cap max_batch_size on realtime pool 1024 -> 256
- offload payloads with >4096 tokens to dedicated-async pool
- enable a tiny canary stream fallback for very-high-latency flows

maria infra: applying rate-limit rule now. command: 
```
redwoodctl policies set-rate-limit --policy free-tier --qps 0.6 --duration 15m
kubectl exec rl-ctrl-0 -- curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/update -d '{"policy":"free-tier","qps":0.6}'
```

maria infra: rate-limit pushed, edge propagated. observed ~40% drop in free-tier qps.

sam oncall: lee, confirm the exact pool patch commands for batching params?

lee ml-runtime: set these on realtime pool: 
```
redwoodctl pools patch realtime --set continuous_batching.window_ms=8 --set continuous_batching.max_batch_size=256
redwoodctl pools patch realtime --set continuous_batching.max_wait_ms=60
```

maria infra: rolling config via configmap patch to avoid full restarts: 
```
kubectl -n inference patch configmap realtime-batching --patch '{"data":{"window_ms":"8","max_batch_size":"256","max_wait_ms":"60"}}'
kubectl rollout restart deployment/realtime-router -n inference
```

ops-bot: :gear: config rollout started for deployment/realtime-router (uid: d3f4...).

alex support: flagging affected accounts with long-poll connections; sending heads-up to top-10. drafting status message.

jo product: adding mitigation note to timeline: rate-limit + batching tuning + offload routing.

sam oncall: adding offload rule for >4k contexts:
```
redwoodctl routes add-offload --from route:/v1/generate --if "payload.context_tokens > 4096" --to pool:dedicated-async --policy async-fallback
```

maria infra: offload rule applied. expect ~10% reduction on realtime pool load.

sam oncall: monitoring metrics; p95 before = 1200ms. check after rate-limit + batch change?

lee ml-runtime: p95 dropped to ~420ms within 90s. queue depth down ~65%. GPU utilization normalized on most shards.

sam oncall: sweet. any client errors? alex?

alex support: small spike in 429s for free-tier immediately after rule — expected. no paid-customer errors reported. support note queued.

lee ml-runtime: note: reducing max_batch_size may remove some kernel-level ams optimizations; watch throughput. if overall throughput drops >20% we may need selective routing changes.

jo product: should we disable model-4-small-quant fallback that increases kernel variance?

sam oncall: good point. disabling fallback only for realtime route: 
```
redwoodctl models patch model-4-small --set routing.fallback.enabled=false --scope route:/v1/generate
```

maria infra: fallback disabled on realtime nodes.

ops-bot: :white_check_mark: requested config changes applied (rate-limit, batching params, offload rule, fallback disabled). suppressing noisy alerts.

sam oncall: i need to step away in ~10m. @lee, please take handoff. key watch items: p95, free-tier 429s, throughput regression. keep batching window at 8ms and max_batch_size 256 for now. if p95 < 500ms for 30m, gradually relax rate-limit to 80%.

lee ml-runtime: taking handoff. creating snapshot and canary metrics.
```
redwoodctl snapshots create --name incident-1905000000 --components pools,routes,models
```
maria infra: snapshot saved: incident-1905000000.

sam oncall: final quick metrics at 09:46 UTC: p95=380ms, p50=95ms, error-rate back to baseline. leaving mitigations in place for observation. if stable for 2 hours we rollback soft rate-limits and re-evaluate batch caps.

lee ml-runtime: filing follow-ups: root-cause (autoscaler -> batching controller interaction), per-customer batching knobs, alert for batch_wait_ms, runbook improvement.

alex support: status page updated: "Partial degraded performance for non-paid tiers; mitigations applied" with timeline link.

sam oncall: good job team. clean mitigation and handoff. leaving channel open for any regressions. :pray:
